name: Zinc
rangeNote: No default range: cut-offs for low zinc depend on age, sex, the time of day and whether the person had eaten, and labs use their own limits. Blood zinc is a limited measure of zinc status: it is affected by recent meals, the time of day, inflammation and some medicines and hormones, and a normal result does not rule out a shortage. µg/dL to µmol/L uses the atomic weight of zinc (65.38).
summary: Zinc is a trace mineral needed for immune function, wound healing, taste and many enzymes. The blood level is a rough guide to zinc status, not a precise measure.

high.meaning: A high zinc level is uncommon. It usually results from high-dose supplements, and long-term excess can lower copper and affect blood counts and immune function.
commonCauses: High-dose zinc supplements, lozenges or denture creams

low.meaning: A low zinc level can come from low intake, poor absorption or losses, and also from inflammation, which temporarily lowers blood zinc without a true shortage. It is read together with symptoms such as poor wound healing, hair loss, frequent infections or loss of taste.
commonCauses: Low dietary zinc, or diets high in phytate that reduce absorption
Digestive conditions that reduce absorption (e.g. coeliac or inflammatory bowel disease)
Acute illness or inflammation (lowers blood zinc temporarily)
Heavy alcohol use or liver disease
